title: Keysmith — Keyboard Layout Lab
description: Rearrange a 30-key board, score it against a real corpus, let an annealer beat your attempt, then drill the result.
concept: Keysmith turns the endless QWERTY-versus-Colemak argument into something you can measure. Tap two caps to swap them and six metrics recompute instantly from a real text corpus: finger travel in metres per thousand characters, same-finger bigrams, home-row share, hand alternation and pinky load, all rolled into one score where QWERTY is pinned at 100. Lock the keys your muscle memory refuses to give up, hit Optimise, and 9,000 simulated-annealing steps rearrange everything else around them. Then switch to Drill and actually type the layout you just invented — the board shows your caps while expecting the physical key underneath, so you can learn positions without remapping your operating system.
features: Design tab: tap-to-swap cap editor with per-key locking, six presets (QWERTY, Dvorak, Colemak, Colemak-DH, Workman, Norman) and a frequency heatmap
Simulated-annealing optimiser — 9,000 chunked steps that respect locked keys and animate the board as it searches
Analyze tab: bigram-flow arcs drawn over the board, eight-finger and three-row load charts, worst same-finger bigram table with reach in millimetres
Compare tab: every preset plus yours across six sortable metrics, best-in-column highlighted
Drill tab: a real typing test on your own layout with live WPM, first-try accuracy, an error heatmap and a per-layout best saved locally
Four corpora including a paste-your-own box, so the ranking is recomputed against the text you actually type
Export a heatmapped PNG card, a JSON report with every metric, or a share link that carries the layout in the URL hash

interaction.mouse: Hover a cap for its finger and row; drag-free tap-to-select, second tap swaps.
interaction.click: Tap two caps to swap them, Lock mode pins a cap, Optimise anneals the rest around it, column headers sort the comparison.
interaction.touch: Every control is tap-sized; in Drill the on-screen caps are the input, so the whole app works on a phone.
interaction.keyboard: In Drill, type the physical key at the highlighted position — Enter starts the next run.
